results.name: Cassoulet de Toulouse
results.locality_or_neighbourhood: Rue Bayard, city centre (near Gare Matabiau)
results.why_it_is_special: A Toulouse institution since 1873, originally stables for the Capitouls then a coaching inn. Widely regarded as the reference for cassoulet in the city — slow-cooked white beans, duck confit, pork, and saucisse de Toulouse in an earthenware cassole.

results.name: Saucisse de Toulouse
results.locality_or_neighbourhood: Saint-Cyprien, left bank of the Garonne
results.why_it_is_special: Buy the sausage fresh and uncooked from artisan charcutiers at this neighbourhood market. The authentic saucisse is coarse-ground pork shoulder seasoned with garlic and pepper, and has held a Label Rouge since 1992. Grill it at home or ask a market vendor to point you to a nearby grill spot.

results.name: Violettes de Toulouse
results.locality_or_neighbourhood: 10 Rue Saint-Pantaléon, historic centre (near Place du Capitole)
results.why_it_is_special: A specialist boutique dedicated to Toulouse's floral emblem. Crystallised violets date back to the 19th century, when nomadic traders brought wild violets from the Tarn-et-Garonne to the city's markets. The shop stocks candies, liqueurs, jams, and cosmetics — all violet-based.

results.name: Fénétra
results.locality_or_neighbourhood: 2 Rue Ozenne, Carmes quarter (also at 3 Place du Capitole)
results.why_it_is_special: A Toulouse pâtisserie founded in 1967, now with seven shops across the city. Fénétra is a medieval-origin tart layered with shortcrust pastry, almond cream, candied apricot, and candied lemon — traditionally baked for the Fête de la Fénétra in late June. Maison Pillon prepares it canonically, as it has been made for decades.

results.name: Magret de canard
results.why_it_is_special: A bistro celebrated for its south-west French produce, sourcing duck directly from farms in the Gers — the very region where chef André Daguin "invented" the magret in the 1960s. The breast is scored, pan-seared until the skin is crispy, and served pink, often with seasonal accompaniments. Pair it with a Fronton or Madiran red.
